Creative Chitti has buttons +1, +10, +100, +1000, +10000. (a) Write two different ways to get 8300. (b) Find the fewest clicks for 8300 and 40629 and write the expressions. (c) What connection do you see between a number and its fewest clicks?
qs.ans: (a) (8 × 1000) + (3 × 100); (5 × 1000) + (33 × 100) (2 marks). (b) 8300 = (8 × 1000) + (3 × 100): 11 clicks; 40629 = (4 × 10000) + (6 × 100) + (2 × 10) + (9 × 1): 21 clicks (2 marks). (c) Fewest clicks = sum of the digits, which is the place value form (1 mark).

qs.q: Which numbers have all five nearest neighbours (thousand to crore) equal to 5,00,00,000? How many are there?
qs.ans: Nearest thousand must be 5,00,00,000, so the number is within 500 of it (1 mark): from 4,99,99,500 to 5,00,00,499 (1 mark). These also round to 5,00,00,000 at every larger place; there are 1000 such numbers (1 mark).

qs.q: Strike out 10 digits from 12345123451234512345 so that the remaining number is as large as possible. Explain.
qs.ans: Pick the largest possible digit each time while leaving enough digits: first 5 (5th digit), then 5 (10th digit) (1 mark), then 3 (13th digit), then the last seven digits 4512345 must stay (1 mark). Answer: 5534512345 (1 mark).

qs.q: Heights: bald eagles fly 4500–6000 m, Mount Everest is 8850 m, aeroplanes fly 10,000–12,800 m. Somu’s building is 40 m. (a)–(c) How many times the building height is each? (d) Which is about 221 times? (e) How many 4 m floors make Everest’s height?
qs.ans: (a) Eagles: 4500 ÷ 40 = 112.5 to 6000 ÷ 40 = 150 times (1 mark). (b) Everest: 8850 ÷ 40 ≈ 221 times (1 mark). (c) Planes: 250 to 320 times (1 mark). (d) Mount Everest (1 mark). (e) 8850 ÷ 4 ≈ 2212 floors (1 mark).

qs.q: Roxie says the product of two 2-digit numbers is always a 3- or 4-digit number. (a) Is she right? Explain using the smallest and largest cases. (b) Can 3-digit × 3-digit give a 4-digit number? (c) Can 4-digit × 2-digit give a 5-digit number? (d) Complete: 8-digit × 3-digit = __ or __ digits.
qs.ans: (a) Yes: smallest 10 × 10 = 100 (3 digits); every product is less than 100 × 100 = 10,000, so at most 4 digits (2 marks). (b) No: at least 100 × 100 = 10,000 (1 mark). (c) Yes: 1000 × 10 = 10,000 (1 mark). (d) 10 or 11 digits (1 mark).

qs.ans: (a) 4 + 5 + 6 + 2 + 6 = 23 (1 mark). (b) 421019 (1 mark). (c) Use the most digits: twelve 1s, 111111111111 (1.5 marks). (d) Fewest digits (4), smallest lead 2: 2008 = 5 + 6 + 6 + 7 = 24 (1.5 marks).
